subject: Dedicated commit query: steady inference for document-search (Alethea Systems)
messages:
From: Emma Conway <emma@alethea.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@alethea.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit query: steady inference for document-search (Alethea Systems)

Hi Sean —

Thanks for taking a look. Quick background: we run a document-search product with ~45M monthly queries today, but the portion we want to move to Redwood Dedicated is our "semantic search" indexer + reranking path (~1.2M reqs/month). Typical request profile:
- average prompt length: ~1.2k tokens (user query + 6 context passages)
- average generated tokens per request: 12
- concurrency at peak: 220 concurrent requests (global)
- p95 latency target: <250ms for 90% of requests

We're evaluating a 12–18 month reserved commit and want guidance on GPU pool size, throughput guarantees, and typical discount bands for this usage. Also curious about burst capacity and fallback levels if we hit unexpected surges.

Can you share a preliminary sizing and a sketch of contract/discount options so we can land this into procurement?

—Emma
Head of Infrastructure
Alethea Systems

Attachments: alethaea_usage_export.csv (CSV export of sample traffic)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Conway <emma@alethea.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@alethea.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit query: steady inference for document-search (Alethea Systems)

Emma — thanks for the context and the sample export. Quick take below; I'm looping Karthik (pricing) and Marcus (capacity) to flesh out a formal proposal.

High-level assumptions I used from your notes + CSV:
- 1.2M monthly inference requests mapped to 40 qps steady state, with 220 concurrent at peak
- Context length ~1,200 tokens; model mix assumed: 70% open-medium / 30% open-large equivalent
- Generated tokens small (12), so token generation cost is minimal vs. KV/cache hit and attention compute

Preliminary sizing (very conservative):
- GPU pool: 6x H100-ish equivalent (packed across pods) for sustained 40 qps with target p95 <250ms and 220 concurrent buffer using our continuous batching profile
- Burst capacity: 2 additional burst nodes (auto-burst) that can spin up within 90s — recommend a guaranteed throughput of 50 qps with a burst allowance to 120 qps for brief windows
- Suggested commit: 12-month reserved pool (6 GPU equivalent) + pay-as-you-go burst credit pool

Questions for you:
1) Do you have a hard requirement on p99 or SLOs tied to uptime?
2) Is colocated regional preference (we assume us-west) or multi-region?

I'll get a detailed cost/discount grid and a short runbook for MS adoption. Marcus/Karthik — can you confirm the GPU equivalence above and a draft price ladder?

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Alethea — workload CSV and ask (please review)

Folks — forwarding Emma's CSV (attached locally as alethaea_workload_profile.csv) and my notes above. Key asks from procurement: 12–18 month reserved commit, prefer predictable monthly spend, and they want a break-glass on burst for seasonal spikes (product launches).

Please:
- Marcus: validate the 6x H100 equivalent estimate and recommend a packing layout that supports fast KV access for 1.2k token contexts.
- Karthik: draft 2 pricing options: (A) 12-month reserved at X% discount with a small burst credit pool; (B) 18-month tiered commit with a higher discount and a defined surge insurance credit. Also include an example of credits given for early termination / SLA credits.

We need a single-slide summary + a one-page contract language summary by EOD tomorrow for the Alethea procurement team.

Thanks — Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Alethea — workload CSV and ask (please review)

Quick numbers after modeling their CSV and our throughput curves. I ran both a conservative and an optimized profile:

Option 1 — Conservative (recommended for first 12 months):
- Pool: 6 GPU-equivalent (H100 class)
- Sustained throughput guarantee: 50 qps (covers steady + reasonable growth)
- Burst credits: 1200 credits/month (credits map to GPU-minutes; enough for ~2–3 large product headlines/month)
- Pricing: list-price equivalent = $XXk/month; reserved 12-month discount = 22% (final net depends on enterprise add-ons)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime; p95 latency target maintained per-route. SLA credits: standard sliding scale (3% credit for <99.9 to 99.5)

Option 2 — Optimized (18-month):
- Pool: 5 GPU-equivalent with tighter packing + quantization (works if they're willing to accept modest 10–12% quality delta on the heaviest requests)
- Sustained throughput: 48 qps with burst to 140 qps using pre-warmed standby nodes
- Pricing: list-price equivalent = $YYk/month; reserved 18-month discount = 32% with a step-up rebate schedule at 12 months if usage grows >15%
- Pilot credit: we can offer a 4-week pilot (up to $10k credit) to validate the packing approach; pilot runs on a mirrored smaller pool

Notes on assumptions:
- Both options assume multi-tenant-safe KV caching and continuous batching tuned for 1.2k contexts.
- If they require strict p99 <600ms we should add 1 GPU-equivalent to either option.

I'll attach a terse proposal PDF for Sean to share (draft name: redwood_pool_proposal_v3.pdf). Marcus — confirm the H100-equivalent mapping and whether we want to propose a regional replication (they asked about global).

—Karthik
Sr. Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Conway <emma@alethea.ai>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@alethaea.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood Dedicated proposal summary & next steps — Alethea Systems (RDW-7782-ALET)

Emma / Carlos — attached is a short proposal and a one-slide summary. TL;DR of recommended pathway:
- Start with Option 1 (12-month reserved, 6 GPU-equivalent pool) to meet p95 <250ms and cover current peak behavior.
- Include a burst credit pool (1200 credits/month) and a 90s auto-burst window to handle product launches.
- Commercials: 22% reserved discount (12-month), included 4-week pilot credit of $10k, and a redwood-managed onboarding package (two SRE days).

Action items for Alethea:
- Confirm region preference (we recommend us-west for latency)
- Agree to pilot window dates (we propose 2027-10-18 — 2027-11-14)
- Procurement asks: target to share PO or preliminary SOW by 2027-10-20

If you want, we can also propose the Option 2 (18-month with deeper discount) but we flagged the model-quality tradeoffs.

Attachments: redwood_pool_proposal_v3.pdf
Link: Shared playbook - https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-example-shared-playbook

Looking forward to your thoughts — happy to hop on a 30m run-through with your SRE/Procurement.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated proposal summary & next steps — Alethea Systems (RDW-7782-ALET)

Sean — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. We're encouraged by Option 1 as a baseline. Couple of counterpoints from procurement/security:
- Discount: procurement is pushing for a 28% floor on a 12-month commit given they are signing up for reserved capacity and will consolidate three internal projects onto this pool. Can you stretch from 22% to 28% if we commit to a 12-month PO worth $Z?
- Pilot: we accept the 4-week pilot but need it to be in-region and have access to logs for our security team (audit-level logs).
- Burst: can you formalize the surge insurance (how credits are consumed, and whether there's a hard cap) — procurement needs deterministic monthly spend numbers.

I've pasted below Marcus's proposal for reference. We can set a sync next week to finalize PO language.
